conflicts.why: Both select architecture/dependencies/layer-direction: CA-DEP-001 checks every layer and FCIS-DEP-001 only the core layer. Resolving deps.layers to CA-DEP-001 keeps the wider check, which still covers the core.

relations.why: Both select architecture/dependencies/layer-direction: CA-DEP-001 checks every layer and FCIS-DEP-001 only the core layer, so the core check is contained in the wider one.
relations.settle: Resolve deps.layers to architecture/CA-DEP-001; the core-layer check stays covered.

relations.why: Both check imports against the preset layers; DCP-EDGE-001 covers the core layer, which CA-DEP-001 already checks, so one forbidden core edge is reported twice.
relations.settle: Turn DCP-EDGE-001 off while CA-DEP-001 is active, unless its managed-component wording is wanted.

source.locator: ch. 22, The Clean Architecture (The Dependency Rule)
source.paraphrase: Compile-time dependencies run from the outer rings toward the inner ones; inner code never mentions what is declared further out, so policy does not depend on detail.

invariants.why: An inner layer that imports an outer one cannot be tested, reused or kept stable without dragging the details along.
invariants.fixHint: Declare what the inner layer needs as a port in a layer it may import, implement it in the outer layer, and wire both in the composition root the preset declares.
invariants.avoid: Barrels and re-exports that tunnel the same edge, type-only imports, require calls and path aliases that point at the same outer module.

relations.why: Both deny pg, mysql2, mongodb and @prisma/client in the core layer, so one import of those packages is reported twice.
relations.settle: Keep both when each list is wanted; to report once, drop the shared packages from one alias with a packages override.

source.locator: ch. 30-32 (The Database Is a Detail; The Web Is a Detail; Frameworks Are Details)
source.paraphrase: Databases, the web and frameworks are details; the business rules do not know them, and the code keeps them at arm's length behind boundaries it owns.

invariants.why: A framework or ORM type in the core ties business rules to a vendor's lifecycle and to infrastructure every test must then start.
invariants.fixHint: Move the framework or ORM call into an adapter outside the core layers and give the core a port that speaks in domain types.
invariants.avoid: Reaching the same package through require, a literal dynamic import, a subpath or a local barrel.

relations.why: Both count public methods: in use-case files CA-UC-001 allows 1 and SR-WIDE-001 allows 8, so a wide use case is reported by both.
relations.settle: Usually keep both, since CA-UC-001 is the narrower use-case rule; to report once, exclude the use-case globs from SR-WIDE-001.

source.paraphrase: A use case describes one application-specific rule: the input it accepts, the steps it runs and the output it returns, behind a single entry point.

invariants.why: Several entry points in one use case mix scenarios that change for different reasons.
invariants.fixHint: Give each scenario its own use case class with one public entry method; shared steps go to private methods or to the domain model.
invariants.avoid: Second entry points written as public arrow-function properties or static methods.
